Booking an apartment for your group in Osaka? The city stopped accepting new special-zone rental applications on 29 May 2026 and is inspecting rentals more closely, so unlicensed listings can be cancelled at short notice. Here's the 3-step check we'd do before paying 👇

⚠️ IS IT LEGAL?

Short-term rentals in Japan need a registration or a special-zone certification.

Legal hosts must record your passport at check-in.

✅ OUR 3-STEP CHECK

1️⃣ Find the registration or certification number on the listing. No number, no booking.

2️⃣ Expect a passport check. A host who never asks for ID is a warning sign.

3️⃣ Add cleaning fees and taxes for every night before you compare with hotel rooms.

🏠 PRIVATE APARTMENT

Good: one shared living space, a kitchen, a washing machine.

Watch: often one bathroom for four, cleaning fees, self check-in, and some have a minimum stay.

🏨 APARTMENT HOTEL

Good: real beds for four, a kitchenette, a laundry machine, and staff if something goes wrong.

Watch: popular with groups, so they book out early.

🛏️ TWO TWIN ROOMS

Good: two bathrooms, daily cleaning, easy cancellation, often right by the station.

Watch: rooms are compact, and there's no common space to hang out.

✅ OUR TAKE

Two or three nights: two twin rooms near a station are usually the easiest.

Four nights or more: an apartment hotel often wins, because laundry and a living room start to matter.
